alt: Four levels numbered from the bottom: the brain stem (autonomic functions such as breathing), the thalamus (sensory processing), the cerebellum (movement such as crawling and walking) and the cortex (cognition, with front parts maturing into adolescence). Genes set the order; nurture affects how well the brain develops.
caption: Brain stem, thalamus, cerebellum, cortex: genes set the order, nurture shapes how well.

alt: New information meets an existing schema. If it fits, the child assimilates it into the schema. If it does not fit, the child feels uncertain and accommodates, changing the schema or creating a new one.
caption: Assimilate when it fits; accommodate when it does not.

alt: A view from above of two crossing walls making four sections, with two policemen outside whose views cover three sections; the boy doll is hidden in the one section neither can see. Cards give the procedure, the finding that most children hid the boy correctly, the conclusion, and a strength and weakness.
caption: A task that made human sense showed young children are less egocentric than Piaget claimed.

alt: Two columns contrast a fixed mindset (ability is set; avoids challenge, gives up after failure) with a growth mindset (ability can be developed; mistakes are part of learning). Praising ability can encourage a fixed mindset; praising effort and strategy encourages a growth mindset. Self-efficacy and an evaluation follow.
caption: Praise effort and strategy, not ability, to encourage a growth mindset.

alt: Learning styles theory claims teaching should match a preferred style, verbaliser or visualiser. Willingham's criticism: there is little evidence this improves learning; the method should suit the content, such as learning a map visually; and much of what we remember is stored as meaning.
caption: Willingham: suit the method to the content and help pupils think about meaning.

alt: Juice is poured from a short, wide glass into a tall, thin glass and five-year-old Ava says there is more juice now. Three points explain it: she is in the pre-operational stage, she cannot conserve, and she focuses on height and ignores width.
caption: Same amount, different look: a pre-operational child judges by height alone.
